entities.name: Muhammad Tawfiq Sidqi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Muhammad Tawfiq Sidqi was an Egyptian Islamic scholar who argued against the authenticity of hadith. He is remembered today for his argument "that nothing of the hadith was recorded until after enough time had elapsed to allow the infiltration of numerous absurd or corrupt traditions"; and that God had allowed this to happen because the Sunnah of Muhammad as a whole "was only ever meant for the Arabs of the Prophet's time", as only the Quran was necessary for Islam,. Sidqi recanted his position after Rashid Rida opposed his position.
